blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Fashion & Luxury. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Fashion and luxury sell scarcity, story and service: assortment risk (the size-curve problem), authenticity, clienteling quality and channel consistency. Technology must be invisible — but the intelligence beneath it decides which drops pay.

items: Piece allocation to doors by rule of thumb; hero-SKU shortages.
Assortment and buy decisions guess curves; end-of-season markdowns absorb the error.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Agentic Process Automation, Decision Intelligence Systems, Intelligent Document Processing from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Assortment and buy planning, Boutique allocation, Clienteling and CRM) on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — GDPR among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: One automation spine: APIs, events, RPA and agents composable under common control.
Workflows that recover from failure on their own — long-running business processes that adapt, retry and recover without tickets.
Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Piece allocation proposed with sell-through policy (availability up)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Retail & Consumer Goods level this capability reads as: store/DC replenishment with size-curve logic proposed for planner approval (OOS down, overstock down simultaneously). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
